meta.title: What's Next for Crypto? | Drinks With Raoul Pal LIVE November 2, 2026
meta.thread_line: 4 threads · liquidity framework · AI capex can't stop · crypto/Nasdaq stuck · dollar & rates path

snapshot: Raoul Pal's live show, held over student-budget snacks and drinks, applies his **"Everything Code"**: demographics drive debt, debt drives money printing, and **liquidity drives asset prices**.
Liquidity has gone nowhere since July, so **crypto and Nasdaq have gone nowhere**. He expects choppy, frustrating markets for the rest of the year.
AI capex "cannot stop": hyperscalers are funded by 30-65% margins and "infinite demand", so he sees a correction, not a bust. Over-levered data-centre owners without power permits are the weak link.
Financial conditions lead global liquidity by ~1 month and point to another drop in liquidity growth, so the ISM and growth slow; he expects recession talk in early 2027 but no recession.
He sees the dollar in a **counter-trend rally** that should fall back toward **DXY ~93** before the next leg higher; rate cuts are "potentially likely" in 2027.
His own positioning: only **accumulating Bitcoin** at the Feb and later lows this year, changing nothing else.

themes.title: Demographics make debt, debt makes liquidity, liquidity drives prices
themes.lead: Pal's chain of causation: falling labour participation means slower growth, more debt, more money printing, and asset prices that follow liquidity.
bullets: Core chart: **government debt is the inverse of the labour force participation rate**; as growth slows, debt rises to "paper over the cracks."
Printing money to pay for the debt mutualizes the cost via losing about **8% a year** of purchasing power; he puts total liquidity at about **$25.5 trillion** and still climbing.

Growth identity: **GDP growth = population growth + productivity growth + debt growth.** The bet (Kevin Warsh, Trump, Scott Bessent) is that AI and robots act as new "population" and lift productivity.
Evidence he cites: revenue per employee at major tech firms has "gone vertical"; he built his dashboards himself with Claude Code despite never having written code.
Broad liquidity roughly doubled (~12,000 to 24,000) while the Nasdaq went ~9 to 36; the gap is "the compounding of technology." Owning technology and crypto is the whole game.

quote.text: Government debt is the inverse of the labor force participation rate.

themes.watch: Pal sells the dashboard, the Real Vision subscription and *The Everything Code* book the framework is built on, and promotes them throughout the show.

themes.title: AI capex can't stop: nobody can slow down, and demand is infinite
themes.lead: Pal argues the AI buildout is funded by the biggest cash-flow machines in history, so a correction does not mean a bust.
bullets: Race logic: if Google slowed capex, Microsoft is "three years ahead" within a year, because **intelligence per joule doubles every ~4.5 months**. Nobody can leave the game.
Anthropic at the top of the stack shows "the fastest growth of profits to this scale in all of corporate history."
Every layer (TSMC, Nvidia, data centres, hyperscalers, models) earns **30-65% margins**, so "this is not the 2000s all over again."
**Infinite demand:** agents, not humans, are the main consumers of intelligence, and they started the year and are "going exponential."
Weak link: leveraged data-centre owners who **can't get power permits** will be bought by cash-rich rivals. Bottlenecks are energy permits and transformers.
Once those bottlenecks clear, newly built capacity filled with cutting-edge chips produces another step change in intelligence.
Elon Musk is probably ahead on power (Colossus 2, bought a mobile gas business, owns solar), so he can supply compute when others can't and "will probably make supernormal profits for a few years."

quote.text: This is the first infinite demand good that we've ever had.

themes.watch: Pal talks his own book on AI-linked assets and sells research on it; the view is his macro thesis, not a company-level analysis.

names.name: Anthropic
names.blurb: Called the frontier-model leader with unmatched profit growth.

themes.title: Crypto and Nasdaq are stuck because liquidity is stuck
themes.lead: Total liquidity has gone nowhere since July, and Pal expects "pretty crappy markets" this year.
bullets: Narrow liquidity is flat because the **dollar rose, the yield curve flattened and rates went up**, so banks aren't levering fast enough.
**Bitcoin** follows US narrow liquidity; the forward projection "is not going to do great for a bit." Excess liquidity also says not great for a while.
Bitcoin is about **1 and a bit standard deviations oversold** vs its log trend, so it is still cheap; he buys anything below those lines.
Nasdaq vs its log trend was almost 2 standard deviations overbought; he advised being cautious or not adding, expecting a return to fair value, then higher.
Liquidity vs Nasdaq hints at a possible squeeze post-election, then a drop again.
His actions: he **bought only in February and at another low** this year, changed nothing else; "all I do is accumulate."
GMI track record claim: 65% hit rate on every recommended trade since 2005, averaging well over 50% per position.
themes.watch: The 65% hit rate is Pal's own tally of his GMI recommendations; the 2005 start date is as spoken.

names.name: Bitcoin (BTC)
names.blurb: Accumulating at lows; expects poor near-term price action with liquidity flat.

names.name: Gold
names.blurb: Moves with financial conditions; will rally as conditions ease.

themes.title: Another growth dip, then easing: dollar toward 93, rate cuts in 2027
themes.lead: Financial conditions point to a slowdown first, then looser conditions as the dollar and rates fall.
bullets: Financial conditions lead global liquidity by about a month and say another drop in its rate of change is coming; the **ISM follows**, so the business cycle slows.
Oil, the dollar and rates all rose; Nasdaq's 12-month rate of change tracks financial conditions with a **3-month lead**.
He expects recession talk in the first 3-4 months of 2027, but "it's not going to happen at all because nobody can allow it." The capex boom cushions it.
Dollar: **counter-trend rally**, likely a final leg down to the bottom of its range (**DXY ~93**), then another leg lower in his view; the long-term view remains dollar-bullish.
Personal history: in 2011 he moved his business billing and savings into dollars and bought property in a dollar-linked place, a multi-decade call that paid off.
Two-year yield: failed at a prior level; watch for a break of the trend line and a gap close. Gold, the 2-year and the dollar are his three dials.
themes.watch: Pal calls the dollar call "maybe me hoping" and says markets "do things you never expect"; his dollar-bullish history is from 2011.

takeaways.title: Track global liquidity and financial conditions before reading any narrative about prices
Treat the next months as an accumulation window for Bitcoin below its log trend, not a momentum trade
Avoid adding to Nasdaq when it is stretched above its log trend
Separate cash-rich hyperscalers from leveraged data-centre owners without power permits
Use gold as a simple proxy when you can't read financial conditions directly
Watch DXY near 93 and the 2-year yield for the turn to easier conditions

hot_takes.take: This is the biggest race of all time. Nobody can go bust because if Google slowed down their capex then Microsoft...
This is not the 2000s all over again.
I think we're stuck this year with pretty crappy markets.
They're like, it's going to go to recession. They [ __ ] it up and it's not going to happen at all because nobody can allow it to happen right now.
We're at what of total liquidity right now we're about 25 and a half trillion.

claims.claim: Intelligence per unit of energy doubles about every four and a half months.
Markets stay choppy and Bitcoin underperforms for the rest of this year because liquidity is flat.
The dollar index falls back to about 93 before its next leg higher.
Rate cuts are potentially likely in 2027 as the economy slows and the dollar falls.
Recession talk will rise in early 2027 but no recession occurs.
Another drop in global liquidity growth is coming, slowing the ISM.

other_news.title: Pal plans to launch a digital art fund, **Epoch One**, with a management firm "in the next month or so"; thesis is owning the scarcest assets in the crypto economy.
Pal just did a trip from Singapore to northern Zimbabwe, Cape Town and Doha, and had his wisdom teeth out at 58; the show was filmed with student-budget snacks.

Sources referenced: his own X post from the day before on why AI capex isn't going bust, and his Global Macro Investor article on bottlenecks clearing; *The Everything Code* book (endorsements quoted from Peter Diamandis, Mickey Malka, Ahmed Mosc).

glossary.def: Pal's framework linking demographics, debt, liquidity and asset prices.
A measure of how easy credit is; Pal says it leads global liquidity by about a month and the ISM and Nasdaq growth by a few months.
Liquidity in excess of GDP, which Pal says explains speculative assets like Bitcoin.
A long-term price trend line on a logarithmic scale; deviations are measured in standard deviations.
